title: Geometry --- Framed Manifolds of Kervaire Invariant One

blocks.tex: Browder's theorem relates the existence of framed manifolds of Kervaire invariant one to the survival of the classes $h_j^2$ in the Adams spectral sequence. In these statements from \cite{LWX126}, spectra are assumed to be 2-completed, connective, and of finite type. The three statements in this chapter have not yet been formalized.

blocks.title: Framed manifolds of Kervaire invariant one

blocks.label: paper:1.1
blocks.title: A framed manifold of Kervaire invariant one in dimension $126$
blocks.body:
\textit{(From \cite{LWX126}, Theorem 1.1.)}
                          

    There exist framed manifolds of Kervaire invariant one in dimension 126.

comments.author: blueprint-authoring
comments.title: Formal scope and provenance
comments.text:
**Formal scope:** Not formalized: geometric endpoint.

Existence of a framed 126-dimensional manifold of Kervaire invariant one is not yet formalized. The current formal endpoint is nonzero permanence of the standard $h_6^2$ class.

blocks.label: paper:1.2
blocks.title: Dimensions admitting Kervaire invariant one
blocks.body:
\textit{(From \cite{LWX126}, Corollary 1.2.)}
                          
The dimensions that there exist framed manifolds of Kervaire invariant one are 2, 6, 14, 30, 62, and 126.

comments.author: blueprint-authoring
comments.title: Formal scope and provenance
comments.text:
**Formal scope:** Not formalized: geometric endpoint.

The complete dimensional classification is not formalized. The repository has no public manifold-existence theorem or exclusion theorem covering precisely these dimensions.
